definition: An emergency fund should cover true income disruptions and unexpected expenses without forcing asset sales.
tip: Target 3–6 months of *essential* expenses, not total spending, and keep it in a high-yield savings account.

definition: Financial decisions should be based on your marginal tax rate, not your average rate.
tip: Evaluate raises, bonuses, and deductions using the tax rate on your *next* dollar earned.

definition: Choosing between Roth and pre-tax accounts depends on current vs future tax rates.
tip: If your current marginal rate is lower than expected retirement rates, Roth usually wins.

definition: Fund fees compound negatively over time, reducing long-term returns.
tip: A 0.75% higher expense ratio can cost over 20% of total returns across 30 years.

definition: Taxable brokerage accounts are best suited for tax-efficient investments.
tip: Favor index ETFs and long-term holdings to minimize taxable distributions.

definition: Early losses in retirement have outsized impact on portfolio longevity.
tip: Hold 1–3 years of spending in cash or bonds to avoid selling stocks in downturns.

definition: Automation removes emotional bias and timing errors from investing.
tip: Automate contributions immediately after payday to enforce consistency.

definition: Every financial choice trades off against an alternative use of money.
tip: Evaluate large purchases by asking what that money could earn if invested instead.

definition: Spending often rises with income unless actively constrained.
tip: Cap lifestyle upgrades to a fixed percentage of raises to preserve savings growth.

definition: Returns depend more on asset allocation than individual security selection.
tip: Choose an allocation you can stick with during market stress—not just bull markets.

definition: Rebalancing enforces buy-low, sell-high behavior.
tip: Rebalance annually or when allocations drift more than 5 percentage points.

definition: Realizing losses can offset gains and reduce taxable income.
tip: Harvest losses opportunistically, but avoid violating wash sale rules.

definition: Capital gains are taxed differently based on holding period and income.
tip: Delay selling appreciated assets until they qualify for long-term gains when possible.

definition: Recurring small expenses often go unnoticed but compound over time.
tip: Audit subscriptions quarterly and cancel anything unused in the last 30 days.

definition: Inflation erodes purchasing power over time.
tip: Ensure long-term investments include growth assets that outpace inflation.

definition: Sinking funds smooth predictable future expenses.
tip: Use sinking funds for travel, insurance premiums, and annual fees.

definition: Credit scores are sensitive to how much of your available credit you use.
tip: Keep utilization below 30%, and under 10% for optimal scores.

definition: Higher deductibles reduce premiums but increase short-term risk.
tip: Choose deductibles you could cover from cash without stress.

definition: Excess idle cash reduces long-term portfolio returns.
tip: Invest surplus cash beyond emergency reserves according to your plan.

definition: Net worth provides a clearer financial picture than income alone.
tip: Track net worth quarterly to monitor progress without daily noise.

definition: Not all debt is equally harmful.
tip: Prioritize paying off high-interest consumer debt before investing aggressively.

definition: Investor behavior often causes worse outcomes than market volatility.
tip: A simple plan you follow beats a perfect plan you abandon.

definition: Employer retirement matches provide guaranteed returns.
tip: Always contribute enough to capture the full match before other goals.

definition: Funds may deviate slightly from their benchmarks.
tip: Small tracking error is normal; persistent underperformance is not.

definition: Buffering protects against short-term cash flow disruptions.
tip: Maintain at least one month of expenses in your checking account.

definition: Delaying consumption increases future financial flexibility.
tip: Implement a 48-hour rule before major discretionary purchases.

definition: Ability to take risk differs from emotional comfort with risk.
tip: Base allocation on capacity first, tolerance second.

definition: Income timing can affect taxes paid.
tip: Shift income or deductions across years to avoid unnecessary bracket jumps.

definition: Separating goals prevents short-term needs from disrupting long-term plans.
tip: Use distinct accounts for short-, medium-, and long-term goals.

definition: Illiquid assets can’t be easily sold without losses.
tip: Balance illiquid investments with sufficient liquid assets.

definition: Money is fungible, despite how we label it.
tip: Evaluate spending decisions based on total financial impact, not account labels.

definition: Small salary increases compound across an entire career.
tip: Negotiating early has disproportionate lifetime payoff.

definition: Nominal returns ignore inflation.
tip: Evaluate long-term plans using inflation-adjusted returns.

definition: Excess emergency cash can hinder growth.
tip: Once stable, redirect excess emergency funds into investments.

definition: Different account types offer flexibility in retirement.
tip: Maintain a mix of taxable, tax-deferred, and tax-free accounts.

definition: Small barriers discourage good habits.
tip: Make saving automatic and spending intentional.

definition: Bonuses and equity compensation have tax implications.
tip: Understand vesting schedules and tax treatment before spending proceeds.

definition: Bond prices move inversely with interest rates.
tip: Match bond duration to your time horizon.

definition: Different goals require different risk profiles.
tip: Avoid investing short-term goals in volatile assets.

definition: Redundancy reduces fragility.
tip: Maintain multiple income streams or employable skills.

definition: Money should reflect personal values.
tip: Spend freely on priorities and ruthlessly cut the rest.

definition: Small filing errors compound into penalties.
tip: Double-check basis tracking and carryforwards each year.

definition: Outliving assets is a core retirement risk.
tip: Plan for longer-than-average life expectancy.

definition: Savings rate matters more than investment returns early on.
tip: Focus on increasing savings rate before optimizing investments.

definition: Time is the most powerful investing variable.
tip: Starting early beats higher returns later.

definition: Too many choices degrade decision quality.
tip: Standardize financial decisions wherever possible.

definition: Complexity increases maintenance errors.
tip: A small number of diversified funds is usually sufficient.

definition: Certain assets perform better during inflationary periods.
tip: Include equities and real assets for long-term inflation protection.

definition: Irregular spending disrupts cash flow.
tip: Smooth expenses with sinking funds.

definition: Skills and reputation drive future earnings.
tip: Invest in learning that increases long-term income power.

definition: Slack provides resilience and optionality.
tip: Aim for buffers beyond the minimum when possible.

definition: Spending later can produce greater satisfaction.
tip: Delay luxury purchases until they feel trivial to afford.

definition: Overexposure to one asset increases downside risk.
tip: Avoid letting any single holding dominate your net worth.

definition: Cash flow drives short-term stability.
tip: Monitor monthly inflows and outflows, not just balances.

definition: Over- or under-withholding affects cash flow.
tip: Adjust withholdings annually after major life changes.

definition: FI depends on expenses more than income.
tip: Lowering annual spending reduces required portfolio size dramatically.

definition: Not all upgrades are equal.
tip: Upgrade things that improve daily life, not status signaling.

definition: Biases distort financial decisions.
tip: Pause before acting during market extremes.

definition: Even spending improves financial stability.
tip: Avoid large discretionary swings month to month.

definition: Every asset eventually gets sold.
tip: Consider liquidity and tax implications before investing.

definition: Automation still needs oversight.
tip: Review automated systems at least annually.

definition: Variable income requires stronger buffers.
tip: Increase emergency savings if income is unpredictable.

definition: High income doesn’t guarantee wealth.
tip: Track assets and liabilities, not just paychecks.

definition: Flexibility increases long-term options.
tip: Avoid financial commitments that lock in high fixed costs.
